parsed.why: No trans-specific offence: 2019 same-sex ban repealed 2020, constitutional privacy, no state-sponsored harassment of the group. But no gender-identity protection or recognition, occasional police 'modesty' charges against gender-nonconforming people, common individual harassment; trans-specific record thin, silence not safety.

Sodomy statutes still in force (dead letter, but police lever). Documented routine police detention on pretexts, extortion, and a 2025 finding of nonconsensual procedures and court-ordered 'gender determination' in custody; bathroom and cell-placement doubt. Courts grant relief, but violations recur.

No trans-specific offence, but public acceptance very low (5/100; 70% call LGBT 'strange'), 2024 rights report documents discrimination, degrading treatment, sexual violence and extortion, hate-crime protection ambiguous, no anti-discrimination law, slow police response: hostile society, thin recourse.

No gender-identity offence; court-ordered recognition, third-gender markers, pride parades, school curriculum: documented acceptance. But a 2024 provincial report documents discrimination plus physical and sexual harassment, and politicians' hostility (2024 rally, 2026 hate speech); courts do grant relief.

No criminalisation and a 2018 constitutional equality guarantee (sexual-orientation ground), with no documented police, border or violence targeting. But no gender-identity provision or recognition procedure documented, and only dated mid-2010s stigma: no confirmed acceptance, so below dossier 4.
